title_en: Why Markets May Be Pricing in Too Many Fed Rate Hikes
title_zh: 为什么市场可能定价了过多美联储加息？ | Robert Kaplan, Goldman Sachs
subtitle_zh: 前达拉斯联储主席解析加息路径、AI 热潮下的货币政策两难与美联储独立性。
summary_zh: 本期 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 由 Allison Nathan 对话 Goldman Sachs 副董事长、前达拉斯联储主席 Robert Kaplan，核心议题是：在新任主席 Kevin Warsh 领导下美联储三年来首次加息后，市场是否定价了过多的后续加息。Kaplan 认为 9 月出手是对的——环比通胀依然接近 3%、油价从一年前 60 多美元升至接近 100 美元，但他倾向 10 月按兵不动、12 月再评估，两次加息即把联邦基金利率（Fed funds rate）推到 4%–4.25%，接近他估算的名义中性利率（neutral rate）。他判断点阵图（dot plot）反应相当克制，因为 AI 基建与应用支出蓬勃，而汽车、住房、面向中低收入消费者的利率敏感部门并不过热，两股反向力量交织。他直言市场预期的加息次数超过实际会发生的，背后是对 Warsh 反应函数（reaction function）不确定、伊朗战争与油价长期高企的风险溢价定价。节目还谈到 10 年期国债突破 5%、Congressional Budget Office 上调赤字预估、缺乏财政整顿对长端收益率的推动，以及本轮'低招聘、低解雇'就业市场叠加多轮供给冲击（supply shock）与历史级资本开支（capex）热潮的罕见组合。是一堂解读'美联储被市场推着走'的货币政策课。
description: Why Markets May Be Pricing in Too Many Fed Rate Hikes

turns.en: The Fed has just raised interest rates for the first time in three years, so was one increase enough to bring inflation down, or should investors expect more rate hikes ahead?
turns.zh: 美联储三年来首次加息，那这一次够不够把通胀打下来？投资者是不是该预期后面还有更多轮加息？

turns.en: I'm Allison Nathan and this is Goldman Sachs Exchanges. Today we're unpacking what this shift means for companies, for interest rates, and for confidence in the Fed, with Goldman Sachs vice chairman and former Dallas Fed president Robert Kaplan.
turns.zh: 我是 Allison Nathan，这里是 Goldman Sachs Exchanges。今天我们请到了 Goldman Sachs 副董事长、前达拉斯联储主席 Robert Kaplan，来解读这轮政策转向对企业、利率以及对美联储信心意味着什么。

turns.en: Rob, welcome back to Exchanges. Good to be here. I'd treat to have you actually in the studio this time around. So as I just said, we have seen the first hike from the Fed in a number of years under new chairman Kevin Warsh.
turns.zh: Rob，欢迎回到 Exchanges。很高兴再次做客。这次我真希望能在演播室跟你面对面。就像刚才说的，在新任主席 Kevin Warsh 领导下，美联储多年来第一次加息了。

turns.en: What was your first reaction to that? Did you think that was the right move? I did think it was the right move. Remember, the Fed did three cuts in the fall of 25.
turns.zh: 你当时的第一反应是什么？你觉得那是对的吗？我确实认为那是对的一步。要知道，美联储在 25 年秋天做了三次降息。

turns.en: I would not have done the third cut. They were worried about the labor market. We then get into 26, we've got tax incentives, we've got an AI infrastructure boom, and then you've got the war with an oil spike.
turns.zh: 第三次降息我本不会做。他们当时担心就业市场。然后进入 26 年，有减税刺激，有 AI 基础设施热潮，再加上战争推高了油价。

turns.en: I think the Fed tried to be patient, tried to see if oil prices were going to settle back down. They haven't. And so I think they were right to do nothing in July, but I did believe that September was the time to act and they did the right thing to raise rates in September.
turns.zh: 我觉得美联储是试着保持耐心，看看油价能不能回落。结果没有。所以我认为 7 月按兵不动是对的，但我也相信 9 月是必须出手的时点——他们加息做了正确的事。

turns.en: But let me ask you a follow up, because did they do the right thing because of inflation concerns or because the market was so convinced it was going to hike that it didn't really have a choice?
turns.zh: 不过让我追问一下：他们加息到底是因为通胀本身的担忧，还是因为市场太确信他们会加息、以至于实际上已别无选择？

turns.en: And is there a difference between those two? Yeah, they had a choice. When you're sitting inside the Fed, I always think I have a choice. And if I think the market is way off, I can go out and communicate and give feedback to the market.
turns.zh: 这两者有区别吗？有的，他们是有选择权的。当你坐在美联储内部，我一直觉得我有选择。如果我认为市场判断太离谱，我完全可以出来沟通、向市场反馈。

turns.en: But the problem was month over month, year over year inflation we know is problematic. I.e., it's in the mid threes, but we understand part of that is oil prices a year ago were in the 60s, they're now close to $100, so that's not a shock.
turns.zh: 但问题是，环比、同比的通胀我们知道是成问题的——同比在百分之三点多的中段。我们理解其中一部分是油价，一年前在 60 多美元，现在接近 100 美元，这确实是个冲击。

turns.en: The thing that was problematic is the month over month numbers. I think they were hoping that those would cool and start to approach, say, 0.2 a month.
turns.zh: 真正麻烦的是环比数据。我觉得他们原本希望环比能降温到大概 0.2%。

turns.en: So annualized 2.5%, let's say. And unfortunately, they ran hotter than that. So even month over month, we're still running closer to three. And I think once they saw that, I believe that it was the right thing to do to start taking action.
turns.zh: 那样年化差不多 2.5%。但遗憾的是，实际跑出来的比这个热。环比依然接近 3%。我觉得他们一旦看到这些数字，就知道该采取行动了。

turns.en: Now the issue is how many times do they need to move? And I think the dot plot, interestingly, was pretty muted, showed a pretty muted response, meaning they're going to raise in September, I think the median was one more increase.
turns.zh: 现在的问题是，他们到底需要加几次？有意思的是，点阵图（dot plot）显示的反应其实相当温和——9 月加一次，我想中位数预测是再加一次。

turns.en: And then some thought they needed to do a little bit more than that, but I think the median showed they don't take any action in 2027. I would call that a fairly muted response.
turns.zh: 有些人觉得可能还需要更多，但中位数显示 2027 年不会有任何动作。我认为这是相当克制的信号。

turns.en: And the reason it's muted is the AI infrastructure part of the economy and AI adoption part of the economy is booming. There's no question about that.
turns.zh: 之所以克制，是因为 AI 基础设施投资这一块和 AI 应用这一块经济正在蓬勃发展，这一点毫无疑问。

turns.en: This spending, for obvious reasons, is very strong. However, when you look at autos, housing related, companies that sell to low-moderate income consumers, business isn't terrible, but it's pretty sluggish or weak.
turns.zh: 这部分支出——原因很明显——非常强劲。但你看汽车、住房相关、面向中低收入消费者的企业，生意不算差，但确实比较疲弱。

turns.en: So the interest-sensitive parts of the market that are affected by the Fed funds, right, are already, in my opinion, not overheated. And so these cross currents created a more muted response from the Fed.
turns.zh: 所以对利率敏感的、受联邦基金利率（Fed funds rate）直接影响的那部分，在我看来已经不过热了。正是这种反向力量的交织，让美联储给出了更温和的反应。

turns.en: So if you think about the fact that nine of the 10 officials are expecting at least one more hike, is that realistic, or are you saying they need to actually hike more, because the market thinks they're going to hike more?
turns.zh: 那如果十分之九的官员预期至少还会再加息一次，你觉得这是现实的吗？还是说你认为他们其实需要加更多——因为市场已经在预期更多了？

turns.en: The market is anticipating that they're going to hike more. And if I were on the committee, my mindset would be, let's move in September. I would probably be inclined, unless there's a reason to act in October, I'd be inclined to skip October, we'll see if they do, and then look again about moving again in December.
turns.zh: 市场确实在预期他们加更多。如果我在委员会里，我的心态会是：9 月先动。然后除非 10 月有理由行动，我倾向于跳过 10 月——当然会看他们怎么做——然后到 12 月再看是否需要再动。

turns.en: Then I want to take a fresh look and see whether or not we need to do more. The reason two moves resonates with me, that gets you to four, four and a quarter.
turns.zh: 我想重新评估一下是不是需要做得更多。之所以两次加息在我脑子里挥之不去，是因为那样利率就到 4.25% 左右了。

turns.en: There are three and three quarters to four right now. I know Kevin Warsh said he doesn't use the neutral rate, doesn't look at it. And I agree with him, it's not the BL end-all, but it's also, in my opinion, not irrelevant.
turns.zh: 现在是 3.75% 到 4%。我知道 Kevin Warsh 说过他不用中性利率（neutral rate）、不看这个。我也同意它不是万能指标，但在我看来它也不是无关紧要的。

turns.en: I think the neutral rate for me is probably plus or minus one, one and a quarter real, plus the inflation rate. I think the nominal neutral rate is around four, four and a quarter.
turns.zh: 我认为中性利率——我的估算——大概是实际加 1% 到 1.25%，再加上通胀率。我觉得名义中性利率大约在 4% 到 4.25%。

turns.en: So then the question once, if they raise it again in December, we're then at four, four and a quarter, I'm probably in the neighborhood of neutral, maybe I need to do one more to be slightly restrictive, but I don't know that I need to do a lot more than that.
turns.zh: 那如果他们 12 月再加一次，就到 4%–4.25% 了，大概就接近中性了。也许还需要再加一次才能略微具有限制性，但我觉得不需要做太多。

turns.en: The reason, again, I don't know is interest-sensitive parts of the economy are not overheating. And so I'm sensitive to the fact that the one tool I have, the Fed Funds Rate, is potent, but it's not going to slow down the AI infrastructure build.
turns.zh: 原因刚才也说了——利率敏感型经济部门并没有在过热。所以我很清楚，联邦基金利率这个工具虽然有力，但它不会让 AI 基建停下来。

turns.en: It's not going to slow down defense spending. And I'm also aware that we've got this oil shock that maybe gets resolved. I don't know that it will, but if it got resolved, that would also cause me to rethink and I'm aware of that and mindful of it.
turns.zh: 它也不会让国防支出放缓。而且我也知道，如果我们碰上的这波石油冲击能够化解——我不知道会不会——但一旦化解，我也得重新思考，这些我都有数。

turns.en: So just to be perfectly clear, you think the market is pricing in too many hikes at this point? I think the market is, yes, expecting more hikes than at the moment, at the moment I think is likely.
turns.zh: 那就说清楚吧：你认为目前市场定价了过多的加息？是的，我认为市场预期的加息次数，超过了我此刻认为实际会发生的。

turns.en: It's putting in an effect a risk premium maybe for a few factors. So what could those factors be? One maybe they say, I don't understand yet the reaction function of Kevin Warsh and therefore of the Fed.
turns.zh: 这背后是在加入某种风险溢价，可能出于几个因素。那这些可能是什么因素呢？第一，也许他们说，我到现在还没完全搞懂 Kevin Warsh 的反应函数（reaction function）——也就是美联储的反应函数。

turns.en: And so I want to build in some cushion. They may also be building in the fact that maybe we can't find a way to resolve the war in Iran and oil prices stay elevated for much longer than everybody thinks, in which case the curve may be more likely to be higher.
turns.zh: 所以我想留点缓冲。他们可能也在定价另一个事实：也许伊朗战争找不到收场方式，油价长期高企，比所有人预期的都久，那利率曲线可能就会更陡。

turns.en: And the probability that the oil price bleeds into 30 or 40 items increases. And I think the market is pricing in some risk premium that that could happen.
turns.zh: 油价传导到三十或四十项其他商品里的概率也在上升。我觉得市场正在为这个风险定价。

turns.en: Understood. When you think about that decision, what does it tell us about whether the Fed is making decisions without political pressure? We've talked about this in the past.
turns.zh: 了解。说到加息这个决定本身，它怎么反映美联储是否在没有政治压力的情况下做决策？我们以前也聊过这个话题。

turns.en: There were some question marks about the Fed's independence with Chairman Warsh coming in. How confident should markets be in the Fed at this point, in its independence and the process around it?
turns.zh: Warsh 主席上任后，外界对美联储独立性画了一些问号。市场现在应该对美联储有多大信心？包括独立性和决策过程？

turns.en: I'm extremely confident that the folks around the FOMC table are doing their level best without political considerations or political influence.
turns.zh: 我非常确信，围坐在 FOMC 桌旁的人都在竭尽全力不受政治考量或政治影响。

turns.en: They're doing their level best to make their best decision. And so they're not being swayed by political factors. I think that's true of the participants on the committee.
turns.zh: 他们全力以赴做出最好的判断。他们没有被政治因素左右。我认为委员会的参会者确实如此。

turns.en: I think people also want to believe that about Chair Warsh. And I think Chair Warsh wants to demonstrate that. I think the raising rates in September was a positive move forward for him in that regard.
turns.zh: 大家也愿意相信 Warsh 主席是这样。我觉得 Warsh 主席也想证明这一点。我认为他 9 月选择加息，在这层意义上对他来说是个积极信号。

turns.en: It shows he's willing to raise rates. But I think the market's still scrutinizing him a bit. But I can tell you around that table, politics or political pressure is not entering into their decision-making.
turns.zh: 这显示他愿意加息。但我觉得市场还在审视他。不过我可以告诉你，在那张桌子上，政治或政治压力并没有进入他们的决策过程。

turns.en: Got it. Let's talk about the real economy. We obviously have seen this big move up in Treasury yields across the curve really. The 10-year Treasury is now above 5%.
turns.zh: 明白。我们聊聊实体经济吧。我们显然看到国债收益率全曲线大幅上行。10 年期国债现在已经突破 5% 了。

turns.en: What are the implications in terms of borrowing costs? For companies, you talked about the resilience and strength of the AI, but that will impact it.
turns.zh: 这对借贷成本意味着什么？对企业来说——你刚才提到了 AI 领域的韧性，但那也会受到影响。

turns.en: So let's talk about the curve. Let's talk about long-duration bonds, 10 years and longer, even five years and longer. But certainly 10 years or longer are more affected by the national deficit.
turns.zh: 那我们来聊聊收益率曲线（yield curve），聊长久期债券——10 年以上，甚至 5 年以上。但 10 年期及以上肯定更受联邦赤字影响。

turns.en: I think there's a concern. There was a hope that if we grew at 4% to 5.5% nominal this year, which is what we're growing. We're growing 2% in a fraction real and inflation's running, you pick the number, 2.5%, 3% we're running close to 5% nominal.
turns.zh: 我觉得市场有担忧。之前有一种希望：如果我们名义增速达到 4% 到 5.5%——今年确实在这个水平，实际增速 2% 多一点，通胀按你选的数字 2.5% 或 3%，名义增速接近 5%。

turns.en: I think the thought was earlier in the year, if growth was that high, we're going to bend the curve of the deficit. According to the Congressional Budget Office, they've now revised up their estimates and it looks like the deficit's going to be higher and not lower than it was last year.
turns.zh: 我觉得年初时的想法是：如果增速这么高，我们就能把赤字曲线压下来。但根据 Congressional Budget Office 的预估，他们已经上调了估计——赤字不但没降，反而比去年还高。

turns.en: So then the question is why? I think that was a little jarring and makes people think maybe government spending either on defense or the war in Iran or other things is much higher than we realize and it's probably causing the market to be a little bit more discouraged that we've got a grip.
turns.zh: 那问题就是为什么？我觉得这多少有些冲击性，让人们开始想：是不是国防开支、伊朗战争或其他支出远超我们的认知？这可能让市场对'我们掌控住了赤字'这个叙事产生了一些动摇。

turns.en: And the second thing is there hasn't been any fiscal plan announced. There have been bond buybacks announced, but I think the market reaction is that isn't going to solve the problem.
turns.zh: 第二件事是，至今没有宣布任何财政整顿方案。有回购国债的动作，但我觉得市场的反应是：那解决不了问题。

turns.en: It might buy you some time or mitigate it on the margin, but there hasn't been a fiscal plan. And so that's affecting the back end of the curve.
turns.zh: 也许能争取点时间或在边际上缓解一下，但没有财政方案。这影响了曲线的远端。

turns.en: Oil prices being higher has affected the whole curve and the irony of the situation is the most booming parts of the economy. In particular, the AI boom is being done with debt and in some cases equity along the yield curve and that's already priced in, I think more rate increases maybe even than the Fed is going to do.
turns.zh: 油价走高也影响了整条曲线。讽刺的是，经济中最繁荣的部分——尤其是 AI 热潮——是靠债务和股票来融资的，而收益率曲线上已经定价了比美联储实际可能做的更多的加息预期。

turns.en: So that's why you notice the Fed increase rates didn't really have much of an effect on the curve because the curve had already adjusted. So what the Fed is doing really isn't going to slow down the AI build.
turns.zh: 所以你注意到美联储加息对曲线的影响其实不大，因为曲线已经自我调整了。所以美联储做什么，实际上并不会让 AI 建设停下来。

turns.en: The people that I talked to that are being affected are people that borrow at the Fed funds rate and that can be small business. It may be some individuals.
turns.zh: 真正受影响的——我交谈过的人里面——是那些按联邦基金利率借贷的人：小企业、一些个人。

turns.en: It'll be some interest rates sensitive sectors. And I talked to housing companies who are struggling to sell the customers because of high mortgage rates, but they financed their inventory based on short term debt.
turns.zh: 还有一些利率敏感型行业。我跟住房企业聊过，他们在高房贷利率下很难卖房，而他们的库存融资又是基于短期债务的。

turns.en: So they're getting squeezed. And so again, a lot of the interest rates sensitive parts of the economy will get somewhat squeezed by this. But corporate CEOs are not so concerned about the rate.
turns.zh: 所以他们两头受挤。话虽如此，很多利率敏感的经济部门会因此受到一定挤压。但企业 CEO 们其实不太担心利率本身。

turns.en: They are much more focused on being able to issue equity or on the Treasury curve and I would say credit spreads and the Treasury curve been reasonably well behaved and have already adjusted up maybe even more than in anticipation of what the Fed's going to do.
turns.zh: 他们更关注的是能不能发股票，以及国债曲线和信用利差（credit spreads）——我觉得这些表现还算稳定，已经提前上移了，甚至可能比美联储实际要做的还要多。

turns.en: Interesting. You just mentioned a few minutes ago about transparency around the Fed's process and reaction function and that has been a big topic in recent months.
turns.zh: 有意思。你几分钟前提到美联储决策流程和反应函数的透明度，这近几个月来一直是个大话题。

turns.en: What are you seeing in that regard at this point and how concerned are you or is that really not a concern of yours? About the Fed's reaction function?
turns.zh: 你现在在这方面的观察是什么？你对此有多担心？美联储的反应函数——

turns.en: About transparency around it, that the markets feel less knowledgeable about how the Fed is going to respond to that. My advice to listeners would be the following.
turns.zh: 或者围绕它的透明度——是否市场觉得更难以判断美联储将如何回应了。我给听众的建议是这样的。

turns.en: If you listen to the speeches of Fed presidents and the governors, I think those are very true to exactly what they're saying in the room around the table.
turns.zh: 如果你去听各联储主席和理事们的演讲，我觉得那些内容非常真实地反映了他们在那张桌子上的发言。

turns.en: Obviously, the chair is being more careful about talking frequently and he's moderating, he's refining his message. But I actually think if you read Fed speeches from the FONC participants, you got a pretty good feel on the debate around the table.
turns.zh: 显然主席说话更谨慎、频率降低了，他在打磨、精炼自己的信息。但我觉得如果你读 FOMC 参会者的演讲稿，你对桌上的辩论已经有相当好的感知了。

turns.en: Actually, I still think there's pretty good transparency. There's a little bit of question, again, trying to interpret Kevin Warsh. The one other thing that I didn't mention that's related to all this is, and you may have heard me say this before, they're very aware at the Fed the share of GDP going to profit for companies is going up.
turns.zh: 实际上我还是认为透明度相当不错。当然，要解读 Kevin Warsh 多少还有些不确定性。还有一件事，跟这些都相关——你可能听我说过——美联储内部非常清楚，GDP 中流向企业利润的份额在上升。

turns.en: AI is accelerating that. The share going to labor is more muted. That's the other reason why you've got more resiliency among companies and that the prospects for their margins and corporate profits to improve is increasing.
turns.zh: AI 在加速这个趋势。而流向劳动的份额则更温和。这也是为什么企业的韧性更强、利润率和盈利改善的前景越来越好的原因。

turns.en: The prospects for low-modern income workers, if you don't own financial assets, yeah, they're getting gains in labor, but they're struggling to make ends meet.
turns.zh: 但如果你不持有金融资产——中低收入劳动者的前景——是的，工资有增长，但他们仍然入不敷出。

turns.en: That's a little also in the back of the minds of people around the table. How much is that a problem for the Fed versus a problem for the administration and the fiscal side?
turns.zh: 这也多少萦绕在那张桌子旁每个人心里。这对美联储来说有多大的问题？还是说这是政府行政部门和财政端的问题？

turns.en: It is an issue for the Fed to be aware of because that's a somewhat different dynamic. They're used to at the Fed for the last number of decades with a few exceptions.
turns.zh: 对美联储来说确实是个需要意识到的议题，因为这是一个相当不同的动态。过去几十年里——除了少数例外——美联储习惯的是另一套框架。

turns.en: You look, is the labor market overheating? Are a number of hours worked expanding or decreasing? What happened to real wages? Normally, if the unemployment rate were going down and you saw those other variables improving, you would be worried maybe we're overheating and we need to cool it off by raising the Fed's funds rate.
turns.zh: 你看，就业市场过热吗？工时在增加还是减少？实际工资怎样？通常如果失业率在下降、其他变量在改善，你会担心过热，需要通过加息来降温。

turns.en: I think you've got a low-fire, low-higher labor market. You've got a different dynamic here where the labor market is not guiding the Fed right now.
turns.zh: 我觉得现在是一个'低招聘、低解雇'的就业市场。这是一个不同的动态，就业市场并没有在指引美联储。

turns.en: I think this is a infrastructure boom with a supply shock, tariffs, constrained labor, and oil. That's a different kind of setup and that's why they're wrestling with how to understand it and how to correctly respond to it.
turns.zh: 我认为这是一轮基建热潮叠加了供给冲击（supply shock）：关税、劳动力受限、石油。这是一种不同性质的格局，所以他们也在纠结怎么理解它、怎么正确应对。

turns.en: One more question for you related to that, which is there's been a lot of focus on supply shocks being more difficult for the Fed to address and navigate.
turns.zh: 还有最后一个相关的问题——现在大家都关注供给冲击更难让美联储去应对和驾驭。

turns.en: What are the implications for Fed policy makers here? Let's talk about what a supply shock is and I'll give you my own two cents on it. If you have a supply shock and it lasts for two months, then I think the knee-jerk reaction if you're at the Fed is let's just wait and do nothing and we'll look through it.
turns.zh: 这对政策制定者意味着什么？让我们来聊聊什么是供给冲击，我给出我的两点看法。如果供给冲击只持续两个月，我觉得美联储的本能反应就是等等看、按兵不动、我们穿透它。

turns.en: If you have a supply shock on the other hand that goes on for six, seven, eight months and maybe it could go on for a lot longer, what happens is it begins to bleed into 30 or 40 items and then a year or two later you forget how the inflation even started.
turns.zh: 但另一方面，如果供给冲击持续六七甚至八个月，甚至可能更久，那它开始向三十或四十项其他商品传导。一两年后你就忘了通胀最初是怎么起来的了。

turns.en: That's why those who say supply shock, what can a Fed funds rate increase do about it? One thing it can do is prevent the bleed or slow the bleed to 30 or 40 other items and more she even commented on that and it was right to do it in the press conference.
turns.zh: 所以那些说'这只是供给冲击，加息能怎样'的人——加息能做的一件事就是阻止或减缓这种传导。Kevin Warsh 在记者会上也提到了这一点，这是对的。

turns.en: We can't stop the oil shock but we can slow down maybe the transmission to other items and I do think they've realized at this point they need to be focused on doing that.
turns.zh: 我们无法阻止石油冲击，但我们可以减缓它向其他领域的传导。我确实认为他们现在意识到了，需要集中精力做这件事。

turns.en: And it's not just the duration of supply shocks, it is the frequency of them because we obviously had the big COVID supply shock, we have this energy shock now.
turns.zh: 而且不仅是供给冲击的持续时间，还有频率。我们有新冠带来的巨大供给冲击，现在又有这轮能源冲击。

turns.en: And I hate to say tariffs is a supply shock, lack of labor force growth, immigration curtailment is another supply shock. We've got a few supply shocks in the face of a historic capex boom and so that's a set of factors that I'm not sure there's a textbook you read on how to understand how to deal with that.
turns.zh: 我不想把关税说成是供给冲击，但它确实是；劳动力增长不足、限制移民也是供给冲击。我们面对的是多轮供给冲击叠加在一轮历史级别的资本开支（capex）热潮之上——我不确定有哪本教科书教过怎么应对这种局面。

turns.en: Right. Last question for you Rob, we have another Fed meeting coming up as we were discussing about let's say five weeks time, I mean what will you be watching to give you more confidence in your view that they won't move in October and what would convince you that they will?
turns.zh: 好的。最后一个问题，Rob，我们大概还有五周就又到一次 FOMC 会议了——你在讨论中说不确定他们 10 月会不会动。你会关注什么来让自己更确信？什么信号会让你觉得他们确实会加？

turns.en: So as always they'll look at the data but the other thing they need to be doing which is we do naturally here and I do in my job at Goldman, they need to be out talking to businesses and I will tell you businesses are telling me again that if it's interest rates sensitive it's okay not great but they need to be out there and understanding what's going on.
turns.zh: 一如既往，他们会看数据。但另一件他们需要做——我们做、我在 Goldman 的工作也做的事——是出去跟企业交流。我可以告诉你，企业反馈的是：如果是利率敏感领域，还行、不算好。他们得出去实地了解情况。

turns.en: They'll also get a PCE, a price indicator on I believe September 30th and they'll get a CPI in mid-October, they'll watch both of those. My own view is I would prefer to do this gradually because of the mixed factors I talked about and wait till December but if those readings or my sense from talking to context is inflation is firming, accelerating or the CPI or the PCE are worse than I expected that's what
turns.zh: 他们也会在 9 月 30 日左右拿到 PCE 数据——也就是个人消费支出（PCE）物价指标——然后在 10 月中旬看到 CPI。这两个都会盯着。我个人倾向于慢慢来，因为前面说的各种混合因素，等到 12 月再说。但如果这些数据——或者我跟人聊下来的感受——通胀在走强、在加速，或者 CPI、PCE 比我预期的差，那就

turns.en: might tip them to say you know what we better act in October. Thanks very much Rob, always a pleasure talking to you. Thanks Alison. This episode of Goldman Sachs Exchanges was recorded on Tuesday, September 22nd, 2026.
turns.zh: 可能促使他们说'好吧，10 月我们最好出手'。非常感谢你，Rob，每次跟你聊天都很愉快。谢谢你，Allison。本期 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 录制于 2026 年 9 月 22 日，星期二。
